summary: Right-footed soccer instep kick at support-foot plant: left foot planted beside the ball, kicking hip extended and knee folded behind, left arm out wide.

cameras.name: side_low
cameras.text: Ground-level side view: the folded kicking leg and the planted foot beside the ball both read clearly.

cameras.name: front_three_quarter
cameras.text: Goalkeeper-side three-quarter view, ball in the foreground, sharp focus on the ball.

cameras.name: ground_wide
cameras.text: Camera almost on the turf behind the kicker, goal visible in the distance.

rules.why: kicking hip extended up to about 29 deg at the end of the backswing
kicking knee near maximum flexion (about 93 deg in elite adults)
support knee about 26 deg flexion at plant
support foot 27-37 cm beside the ball (best ball speed and accuracy)
support foot level with or slightly behind the ball centre
non-kicking arm abducted and extended (tension arc)

text.action: a soccer player winding up a right-footed instep shot, left support foot just planted beside the ball
text.core: Left foot planted flat beside the ball, about 30 cm to its left and level with it, left knee slightly bent; right kicking leg drawn back behind the body with the hip extended and the knee folded so the heel rises toward the buttock, toes pointed; trunk leaning slightly back and away; left arm stretched out wide and back for balance, right arm swinging forward across the body.
text.gaze: Head down and still, eyes on the ball.
cues: plant the support foot beside the ball, not behind it
kicking knee folds tight, heel toward the buttock
non-kicking arm out wide builds a tension arc across the trunk
approach from about 30-45 degrees to the target line
kinetic: turf and grass blades kicked up behind the plant foot
motion blur on the kicking foot swinging back
shirt twisting with the trunk rotation
avoid: support foot floating or on tiptoe
support foot directly behind the ball
both arms hanging at the sides

sources.cite: Kellis & Katis 2007, JSSM 6:154, biomechanics of the soccer kick (hip extension up to 29 deg in the backswing)
Systematic review of instep-kick kinematics in elite adult players (maximum knee flexion 93 +/- 5 deg)
Lees et al. 2010, J Sports Sci review: support knee 26 deg at plant, 42 deg at contact; pelvis rotates 30-36 deg to contact
Ou, Lei & Cheng, Science and Medicine in Football 7:34-40: support foot beside or slightly ahead of the ball, 27-37 cm to the side
McLean & Tumilty 1993 via Basumatary thesis: support foot about 30 cm to the side and 5-10 cm behind
Shan & Westerhoff 2005, Sports Biomech 4:59-72: full-body tension arc of the maximal instep kick
